comments.author: @BellaEmma1
comments.text:
Singaporeans have NEVER and should NEVER see ourselves as perfect. We have more problems, imperfections, shortcomings, flaws, faults, weaknesses, vulnerabilities, undesirable traits & characteristics than we can count.

Singapore & Singaporeans NEVER asked to be REGARDED as a model or example for other countries.

We NEVER asked to be praised or imitated or copied.

We NEVER wanted/asked for the attention, scrutiny, judgement, assessment or analysis that people & countries give of/about us or how we live our lives.

We're the tiniest city-state in the world, with no natural resources or landscapes or hinterland & when we separated from Malaysia, hardly any means to make a living to survive in this harsh world.

And YET, due to God's Grace, Blessings, Love, Providence, Will, we have not only survived but thrived for over 60 years.

Despite all the criticisms, brickbats, hatred, envy, frustrations, ill-will thrown our way from the entire planet, we are still here & we are still enjoying peace, prosperity, progress, stability, security, comfort that many people around the world DO NOT ENJOY. 

Nothing, nobody, no system, no policy, no country, no leader or leadership, not a single thing in this entire universe IS, or CAN BE, perfect. Only God The Almighty Owns that Accolade. Only God Is Perfect.

Every country has their own problems, shortcomings, flaws, imperfections, weaknesses, vulnerabilities, undesirable traits & characteristics.

Singapore & Singaporeans do not exist or die because of people's criticisms or praises. Only God The Almighty Determines our existence or demise according to His Will. The same applies to every country & every single creation in this entire universe.

I'm a born and raised Singaporean of 56 years and have lived here my entire life & I will probably die here too. There is no other place worthy for me to call HOME, even with all its shortcomings, flaws, faults, imperfections, weaknesses, vulnerabilities, undesirable traits & characteristics because no country, no place, nothing IS, or CAN BE, perfect.

But there is only ONE place one CAN CALL HOME. Home is where the heart is. There's no place like home. There's no place like Singapore for me. But of course, Singapore is NOT for everyone. It's only for those who can appreciate it, be grateful for it & be contented with it. People like me. I appreciate it, am grateful for it & am contented that I've lived here my whole life.

comments.author: @BellaEmma1
comments.text:
Singapore's founding leaders knew that without natural resources or anyone or anything to help us survive expulsion/separation from Malaysia, we had to figure out our own way on how to survive as an independent, sovereign tiny city-state in an unforgiving, unrelentingly challenging & harsh global environment. By God's Grace, they figured it out.

Singapore & Singaporeans NEED to be RELEVANT, USEFUL, ACCOMMODATING & FRIENDLY TO ALL & ENEMY OF NONE.

We can't do what the big countries with vast natural resources, large land mass & huge human resource can do so we figured out what we CAN do with what we DO have & DO & BE THE BEST WE CAN DO & BE in the eyes of the world.

Think out of the box.
Apply what works for others & do it even better.
Learn from the mistakes of others.
Think & plan long-term while working hard for the short- & medium-term.
Never forget that nobody owes us a living & we can't expect help from others when we're in dire straits.

As the saying goes - necessity is the mother of invention.

Singapore took it to another level. We NEEDED to be creative/innovative to SURVIVE. We didn't have a choice. It's either innovate or perish.

By God's Grace, we have survived & thrived. All praises to God The Almighty for His Blessings.

comments.author: @BellaEmma1
comments.text:
To each his own.

Many would disagree that it's one of the best places in the world to live.

Its 24/7 365 days' of heat & humidity with little respite even when it rains.

Its tiny size contributing to a cramped, densely-packed living environment with crowds everywhere we turn especially when taking public transport.

Its lack of natural landscapes such as mountains, lakes, sea & ocean fronts.

Its strict laws, rules, regulations, constraints, control of expression.

Its constant fear of failure & eternal need to be 'exceptional' & relevant because it's a matter of survival & an existential concern, which means, its citizens & residents are pushed to work till we die because people are Singapore's ONLY resource.

But to me as a born & raised Singaporean & have lived here my entire 56 years of life, it's just HOME. Even with all its imperfections, shortcomings, flaws, constraints. I know nobody can tell me to "go back to China/India/wherever I came from" because I came from here. That's something that not even all the money in the world can buy.

comments.author: @BellaEmma1
comments.text:
Perspective.
It's ESSENTIAL.
CRUCIAL.
IMPORTANT.

Singapore is a tiny island.
Smaller than New York City.

Less than 3.7 million citizens.
And slightly less than 3 million permanent residents & foreign workers.

Became a sovereign country in 1965, so only about 60 years of nationhood.

No natural resources.
No hinterland.
No large land mass.
Completely surrounded by seawater.

The entire island can be WIPED OFF the world map by a HUGE TSUNAMI or EARTHQUAKE.

Compare it with :
Its neighbours.
Or the US.
Or China.
Or literally any other country on earth.

Especially those with 100s or 1000s of years of nationhood or civilisation.

Singapore DOES NOT hold a candle to any of them.

We are INSIGNIFICANT.

Please REFRAIN from putting Singapore on a pedestal or INFLATING the potential impact of what Singapore does to the extent that it DOES NOT DESERVE.

Singapore NEVER wanted or asked to be the model or example or ideal for the world to emulate.

Nothing that we have been blessed with can or will last forever.

Everything could disappear in the blink of an eye. If that is God's Will. And there's nothing anyone can do to stop it. That's the nature of this temporary life. Everything will come to an end.

Singaporeans SHUN adulation, admiration, effusive praise or accolades because we don't want to become arrogant, obnoxious, entitled, intolerant, ungrateful, spoiled brats that will cause us to be loathed by the world.

We just want to live peaceful, harmonious, tranquil lives through our hard work & by getting along with everyone as far as possible & be good, useful, productive human beings for the duration of the time we are given in this life.
